channel.title: Secure on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Secure on Best of AI

item.title: Metasploit
item.description:
Testers select an exploit, configure a payload, and run it against a target they have permission to test. The framework includes scanners and post-exploitation modules. Rapid7 maintains it.

A free community edition exists, and Metasploit Pro adds features.

Cobalt Strike and Burp Suite serve other test needs. Metasploit suits penetration testers.

item.title: Nmap
item.description:
Users run scans from the command line or a graphical front end such as Zenmap. The scripting engine adds checks for vulnerabilities and service details. Results export to several formats.

Scanning networks without permission is illegal in many places, so use it only on systems you are allowed to test.

Masscan is faster at scale. Nmap suits penetration testers and network engineers.

item.title: OpenZeppelin
item.description:
The Contracts library offers tested building blocks such as ERC-20 and ERC-721 tokens. A contracts wizard generates starter code. The company also performs audits and offers monitoring tools.

Using audited libraries lowers risk, but custom code still needs review.

CertiK and Trail of Bits offer audits. OpenZeppelin suits blockchain developers building production contracts.

item.title: Recorded Future
item.description:
Analysts look up indicators like domains and hashes, read risk scores, and see related campaigns. Alerts flag leaked credentials and brand abuse. An AI assistant answers questions about reports and threats.

It is an enterprise product, now part of Mastercard, with custom pricing.

Mandiant and CrowdStrike Falcon Intelligence are alternatives. Recorded Future suits threat intelligence analysts.

item.title: Tenable
item.description:
Scanners find missing patches, misconfigurations, and exposed services across servers, cloud accounts, and web apps. Risk scores combine severity with exploit activity and asset importance, and generative AI features summarize attack paths for analysts.

Nessus is widely used for individual scans, while Tenable One targets enterprise programs. Plans and pricing vary.

Qualys and Rapid7 are alternatives. Tenable suits cybersecurity analysts who run vulnerability programs.

item.title: Verkada
item.description:
Staff manage cameras from a browser, search footage by person attributes or events, and get alerts for unusual activity. Access control and visitor management are included. The platform is aimed at schools, offices, and retail.

It is sold with subscriptions to organizations. Privacy and data use rules should be reviewed before deployment.

Rhombus and Avigilon are alternatives. Verkada suits security guards and the teams that manage camera systems.

item.title: VirusTotal
item.description:
Users upload a file or paste a link and see verdicts from dozens of vendors, along with behavior reports and community comments. An API supports automation, and paid plans add search and hunting. AI summaries explain suspicious code.

Uploaded files become visible to others, so sensitive files should not be submitted.

Hybrid Analysis and Any.Run are related tools. VirusTotal suits cybersecurity analysts doing triage.

item.title: Maltego
item.description:
Maltego is known for visual link analysis. An investigator starts with an entity such as a domain name, email address, or company, then runs transforms that pull related data from sources like DNS records, social media, breach databases, and corporate registries. The results appear as a graph that shows how things connect, which makes patterns easier to see than in a list.

The tool is widely used in cybersecurity and open-source intelligence work. Threat analysts trace infrastructure behind attacks, fraud teams look for networks of related accounts, and journalists and researchers map ownership and connections. A marketplace of data integrations extends what the graph can query, and collaboration features let teams share findings.

item.title: Microsoft Security Copilot
item.description:
Security Copilot aims to relieve the pressure on overstretched security operations teams. An analyst can ask in plain language what happened in an incident, and Copilot gathers signals from Microsoft’s security products, summarizes the attack path, explains the alerts, and suggests next steps. It can write queries in languages like KQL, analyze suspicious scripts and files, and produce incident reports, saving time on routine tasks.

The product has moved toward agents. Purpose-built agents handle jobs such as triaging phishing alerts, assessing vulnerabilities, and prioritizing conditions that need attention, working with human oversight. It is embedded in the portals analysts already use, and plugins connect to non-Microsoft tools, so it can use data from other systems. Controls govern what it can access and do.

item.title: Moderne
item.description:
Moderne makes large-scale code change practical. OpenRewrite is an open-source refactoring engine that applies automated recipes to code, such as upgrading Java versions or replacing a deprecated API. Moderne indexes an organization’s repositories and runs recipes across all of them, producing pull requests.

That addresses the problem of maintaining hundreds of services. Instead of each team doing the same migration by hand, a platform team can run a recipe once and review the results. Search and analysis tools find where patterns occur, and AI assists in creating recipes and handling changes that rules cannot.

item.title: Secureframe
item.description:
Secureframe automates compliance work. It integrates with cloud providers, code repositories, identity systems, and HR tools to check that required controls are in place, gather evidence for auditors, and alert teams when something drifts out of compliance.

The platform also manages policies, employee training, vendor risk, and a trust page for customers. AI drafts policies, maps controls across frameworks, and fills in security questionnaires from a company’s own answers, saving time during sales cycles.

item.title: Securiti
item.description:
Securiti addresses the problem that companies often do not know where their sensitive data lives. It scans cloud storage, databases, SaaS apps, and data pipelines, classifies personal and confidential information, and builds a map of where it sits and who can access it. This approach is known as data security posture management.

On top of that, it automates privacy and governance tasks. Teams respond to data subject requests, manage consent, run privacy assessments, and enforce policies that block risky access. For AI, Securiti helps discover models and data feeding them, apply guardrails, and meet emerging regulations, which has become a priority as companies adopt generative AI.

item.title: SentinelOne
item.description:
SentinelOne is a cybersecurity company known for autonomous endpoint protection. Its agent runs on computers and servers, uses machine learning to detect malicious behavior on the device, and can respond automatically by isolating a machine, killing a process, or rolling back changes made by ransomware. That local decision-making works even when a device is offline.

The Singularity platform extends this across the environment. It brings together endpoint detection and response with cloud workload security, identity threat detection, vulnerability management, and a data lake that collects logs from many sources for threat hunting. Purple AI is a generative assistant that lets analysts ask questions in natural language, such as whether a suspicious file appeared elsewhere, and turns them into queries, summarizes findings, and suggests next steps.

item.title: SonarQube
item.description:
SonarQube analyzes source code without running it. It checks for bugs, security vulnerabilities, hardcoded secrets, code smells, duplication, and test coverage, and reports issues in a dashboard and in pull requests. Teams define quality gates, such as no new critical bugs, which can block a merge when code does not meet the standard, so problems are caught early in development.

It integrates with CI/CD systems like GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins, and Azure DevOps, and with IDEs through SonarLint, which highlights issues as you type. AI features include CodeFix, which suggests changes for issues it finds, and capabilities designed to check AI-generated code, an area of growing concern as more code is written by assistants. It supports a large number of languages and frameworks.

item.title: Splunk
item.description:
Splunk made machine data searchable. It ingests logs, metrics, and events from servers, applications, networks, and cloud services, indexes them, and lets users search and visualize with its Search Processing Language. Companies use it to troubleshoot outages, monitor performance, and investigate security incidents, and it has been a mainstay of security operations centers for many years.

The product line includes Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud for core analytics, Enterprise Security as a SIEM for threat detection, and observability tools for infrastructure and application monitoring. AI features include an assistant that helps write searches from plain language and summarizes findings, and machine learning for anomaly detection. Cisco acquired Splunk and is integrating it with its networking and security products.

item.title: OpenAI Daybreak
item.description:
Daybreak gives defenders access to frontier AI for security work. Approved organizations use models for tasks such as triaging incidents, analyzing malware, validating patches, and hunting for vulnerabilities, with workflows designed for security teams.

OpenAI split access into tiers. A defender tier provides frontier models without some of the safeguards that might block legitimate security prompts, and a more specialized tier provides models trained for higher-risk testing such as vulnerability research and exploit validation. Access is limited to vetted individuals and organizations.

item.title: Elastic AI Assistant
item.description:
Elastic AI Assistant is built into the Elastic stack, which many companies use for search, logs, and security monitoring. Users ask questions in plain language, such as what caused a spike in errors or what an alert means, and the assistant queries the data, explains findings, and suggests next steps.

For security teams, it helps triage alerts, write queries, and summarize incidents using the organization’s own data. For observability, it assists with investigating logs and metrics. Retrieval from indexed content grounds answers in real information, and administrators choose which language model provider to connect.

item.title: Palantir AIP
item.description:
AIP, the Artificial Intelligence Platform, is Palantir’s layer for putting language models to work on an organization’s data. It builds on Palantir’s ontology, a structured model of a company’s objects, such as orders, machines, and customers, and the actions that can be taken on them. Models can then read and act within that governed model instead of working on raw text.

Customers build agents and applications that automate tasks, answer questions, and support decisions in areas like supply chain, healthcare, defense, and manufacturing. Controls around access, logging, and human approval aim to make AI usable in sensitive settings. Palantir runs engagement programs that help customers reach production quickly.

item.title: BigID
item.description:
BigID starts with a question many companies cannot answer: where is our sensitive data? It scans databases, file shares, cloud storage, SaaS apps, and data lakes to discover personal information, financial records, and other regulated data, then classifies it using machine learning. The results build a catalog showing what data exists, where it sits, and who can access it. That map is the basis for privacy and security work.

Several functions build on the catalog. Privacy teams use it to respond to access and deletion requests, track consent, and meet rules like GDPR and CCPA. Security teams use it to find overexposed data, fix permissions, and reduce risk through remediation workflows. A newer focus is AI governance: the platform identifies which AI agents, copilots, and models can reach sensitive data, helps limit that access, and checks against frameworks such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the EU AI Act.

item.title: CloudHealth by VMware
item.description: CloudHealth was one of the first tools built for managing cloud costs across several providers. Companies connect their AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud accounts and get a consolidated view of spending, broken down by team, project, or application using tags and rules. Reports show where money goes, budgets raise alerts when spending drifts, and recommendations point to unused resources and oversized instances. That helps finance and engineering teams share a view of cloud costs.

item.title: CrowdStrike
item.description: CrowdStrike’s core product is Falcon, a cloud-based endpoint security platform. A small agent on laptops, servers, and cloud workloads sends behavior data to CrowdStrike’s cloud, where machine learning and threat intelligence look for malicious activity such as ransomware or hands-on-keyboard attacks. Because analysis happens in the cloud, the agent is light and updates quickly. The company’s detection and response model, known as EDR and XDR, is widely used by large enterprises and governments.

item.title: CVAT
item.description: CVAT was created at Intel and released as open source, and is now maintained by a company called CVAT.ai along with a community. It is a web-based tool for labeling data for computer vision: drawing bounding boxes, polygons, polylines, points, and masks, and tagging images or video frames with classes. It handles tasks such as object detection, segmentation, tracking across video, and classification, and exports to common formats such as COCO, YOLO, and Pascal VOC.

item.title: DNAnexus
item.description: DNAnexus gives life science organizations a place to work with very large datasets. Sequencing a genome produces enormous files, and analyzing thousands of them takes substantial computing and careful data management. The platform provides cloud storage, scalable compute, workflow tools, and a catalog of bioinformatics pipelines, so teams can run analyses without managing their own servers. It is built to meet regulatory and privacy requirements for clinical and health data.

item.title: Drata
item.description:
Drata addresses the burden of proving security compliance. Companies selling to enterprises are often asked for a SOC 2 report or other certifications, and preparing for an audit traditionally takes months of gathering screenshots and documents. Drata connects to systems such as AWS, Google Workspace, GitHub, Okta, and HR tools, automatically checks whether controls are in place, and collects evidence continuously, so the company remains audit-ready.

The platform covers more than evidence. It manages policies and employee training, tracks vendor risk, supports risk assessments, and offers a trust center that lets customers see a company’s security posture. Auditors can work directly in the platform. AI features help fill out security questionnaires, summarize risks, and map controls across multiple frameworks, saving time for small security teams.

item.title: Gretel.ai
item.description: Gretel helps teams get usable data when real data is sensitive or scarce. Developers connect a dataset, such as customer records or medical tables, and Gretel trains a model that produces new records with the same statistical patterns but no direct link to real individuals. Teams use the results to test software, share data across departments, and train machine learning models without waiting for privacy approvals. It also generates text and tabular data for fine-tuning language models.

item.title: MOSTLY AI
item.description:
MOSTLY AI helps organizations use data that would otherwise be locked away by privacy rules. It trains a generative model on a real dataset, such as customer transactions or patient records, and then produces a new dataset that reflects the same patterns, relationships, and distributions but contains no real individuals. Banks, insurers, and healthcare companies use it to share data across teams and borders, test software, and develop models.

The platform handles multi-table relational data, preserving links between tables such as customers and their orders. Quality and privacy reports compare the synthetic data with the original and check for leakage, and features can rebalance datasets to reduce bias or fill in rare cases. An open-source SDK allows developers to run generation in their own environment, while the platform adds a user interface, scheduling, and enterprise controls.

item.title: Okta
item.description:
Okta is one of the best-known providers of cloud identity. Companies use it as the central place where employees sign in to their applications: one login gives access to hundreds of apps through single sign-on, and multi-factor authentication adds protection against stolen passwords. The Universal Directory stores identities and groups, and lifecycle management automates giving people the right access when they join, change roles, or leave.

The platform covers more of the identity problem over time. Adaptive policies check device and context before allowing access, governance tools handle access reviews and requests, and privileged access tools protect administrator accounts. Okta also owns Auth0 for customer-facing apps. As companies deploy AI agents that act on behalf of users, Okta has added features for giving these agents their own identities and managing what they may do.

item.title: OneTrust
item.description:
OneTrust helps large organizations manage the rules about data. Its best-known product handles consent: the cookie banners and preference centers that appear on websites and apps and record what visitors agree to. Privacy teams use other modules to respond to data subject requests such as access and deletion, map where personal data is stored, run privacy impact assessments, and show regulators that they follow laws like GDPR and CCPA.

The platform has expanded into broader governance, risk, and compliance. Tools cover third-party and vendor risk, security and IT risk, ethics and policy management, and environmental and social reporting. A growing area is AI governance: inventorying the AI systems an organization uses, assessing their risks, and tracking compliance with emerging rules such as the EU AI Act. AI features in the platform help classify data and automate assessments.

item.title: Osano
item.description:
Osano began with cookie consent, the banner that asks visitors what tracking they accept. Its consent manager scans a site, categorizes cookies and scripts, shows region-appropriate banners, and records choices, which helps companies comply with laws such as GDPR and CCPA. Websites install it with a small piece of code, and it can block scripts until a visitor agrees.

The platform grew to cover the wider privacy program. Tools handle data subject access requests, data mapping, and assessments, and a vendor monitoring service tracks the privacy practices of third parties and flags risks. Osano also offers privacy rating information and a catalog of vendor reports. Features for managing AI use and policies are being added as regulation develops.

item.title: Petcube
item.description:
Petcube sells connected cameras for people who want to check on pets while away. A camera with a wide-angle view streams video to a phone app, and two-way audio lets owners talk to the pet. Models differ in features: some include a built-in laser toy for play, some toss treats on command, and some are designed for indoor or outdoor use. Setup is through Wi-Fi and a smartphone.

Software adds intelligence. AI can detect when a pet is barking, moving, or when a person is in view, and send alerts, and a subscription provides cloud recording, event history, and access to veterinarians by video chat. Pet owners use it to keep an eye on anxious dogs, monitor cats, and share live views with family members.

item.title: Tinybeans
item.description:
Tinybeans is a place to keep a child’s growing-up record. Parents upload photos, videos, and short notes, and they appear in a private timeline organized by date and by child. Selected family members, such as grandparents, are invited to view and comment, which keeps updates off public social networks while sharing moments with those who care.

Features help preserve memories. Milestone tracking prompts parents to note first steps and other events, a calendar shows memories on this day, and storage keeps content safe over the years. A premium plan adds unlimited uploads and the ability to order photo books, calendars, and prints. AI helps organize and suggest highlights.

item.title: Tonic AI
item.description:
Tonic.ai solves a common development problem: engineers need realistic data to test software, but production data contains sensitive information. Tonic Structural connects to a database, identifies sensitive fields, and replaces them with fake but realistic values, preserving relationships and formats so applications behave as they would with real data. This allows teams to build and test with representative data without exposing customers’ details.

Other products broaden the range. Tonic Fabricate generates synthetic data from scratch for new applications or demos, and Tonic Textual finds and redacts sensitive information in unstructured data such as documents and text, which helps prepare data for training or retrieval in AI systems. Integrations support popular databases and data warehouses, and subsetting tools cut large databases down to smaller, usable test sets.

item.title: Transcend
item.description:
Transcend takes a developer-oriented approach to privacy compliance. It connects to a company’s databases, SaaS tools, and warehouses to discover where personal data is stored, then automates responses to requests from individuals to access or delete their data. Instead of manually searching dozens of systems, the platform executes the request across them and keeps a record.

Other products cover related needs. Consent management controls cookies and tracking according to each visitor’s choices and location, a gateway can enforce those choices in what data flows to third parties, and data mapping documents processing activities. Newer tools address AI governance, helping teams track what data feeds models and meet emerging regulations.

item.title: Vanta
item.description:
Vanta helps companies prove they run secure operations. It integrates with tools such as AWS, Google Workspace, GitHub, Okta, and HR systems, continuously checks whether controls like encryption, access reviews, and employee training are in place, and collects the evidence auditors need. This replaces manual screenshots and spreadsheets and keeps a company audit-ready year-round.

The platform has grown into a broader trust management suite. It tracks vendor risk, manages security policies and employee onboarding tasks, runs risk assessments, and provides a trust center where customers can see a company’s security posture. AI features answer security questionnaires, map controls across frameworks, and help prioritize remediation, saving time for small security teams.

item.title: Wiz
item.description: Wiz became one of the fastest-growing security companies by making cloud risk easier to see. It connects to cloud accounts through APIs and snapshots, without installing agents on every machine, and builds a graph of resources, identities, networks, and data. From that graph it finds problems such as exposed storage, over-permissive roles, unpatched software, and secrets in code, and it shows how they could be chained together into an attack path to something valuable.

item.title: Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Bedrock is how many companies on AWS use large language models without running any model infrastructure. Instead of signing separate contracts with each AI lab, you pick from a catalog of models from providers such as Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and Amazon itself, and call them through one API. The data stays inside your AWS account, which matters to teams with security, privacy, and compliance requirements, and it works with the IAM, networking, and logging tools they already use.

item.title: Anytype
item.description:
Anytype is a workspace for notes and structured information built around privacy. Data is stored locally and encrypted, and syncs between devices peer to peer or through backup nodes, so you keep ownership of your content rather than leaving it on a company server. The app is open source.

Its model uses objects and types. Everything is an object, such as a page, a person, a book, or a task, and each type has fields. Objects link to each other and appear in sets and collections, which function like databases. This lets users create a personal wiki or a custom organizer without code. Optional AI features can summarize and help write.

item.title: Apple Maps
item.description: Apple Maps comes installed on every Apple device and has improved a great deal since its rocky start. It provides turn-by-turn driving directions, walking, cycling, and public transit routes, plus lane guidance and speed limit information. Features such as Look Around give a street-level view of many cities, detailed maps show buildings and landmarks in 3D, and downloadable offline maps work without a connection. Guides collect recommended places in a city, and you can share your arrival time with friends.

item.title: AWS GovCloud
item.description: AWS GovCloud is a separate set of AWS regions built for workloads that carry strict regulatory requirements. US government agencies, contractors, and other organizations handling controlled data use it to host systems that must comply with standards such as FedRAMP High, the Department of Defense Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide, ITAR, CJIS, and HIPAA. The regions are physically and logically isolated from the standard AWS regions, and access is restricted to vetted US citizens.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Service
item.description:
Azure OpenAI is OpenAI’s model lineup delivered through Microsoft’s cloud. Companies use it to get the same families of language, reasoning, image, and audio models, but under Azure’s terms, billing, and security controls. For regulated industries and large enterprises, that matters: the data is processed inside Azure, can be isolated on a private network, and is covered by Microsoft’s compliance certifications and service-level agreement.

Development happens in Microsoft Foundry, where you deploy a model, test it in a playground, and connect it to your own data and tools. Available features include fine-tuning, content filtering, tool and function calling, retrieval over company documents, and tracing. Deployments come in several types, such as standard pay-as-you-go, batch, and provisioned throughput, which reserves capacity for steady workloads with predictable latency. Foundry also offers non-OpenAI models, so teams can compare options in one place.

item.title: Bito AI
item.description:
Bito started as a chat and code-completion assistant inside VS Code and JetBrains IDEs and as a command-line tool. You could ask it to explain a function, write unit tests, find bugs, or generate documentation, and it used a model of your choice for the answers. Its early appeal was practical convenience: reusable prompts for common tasks and support for working with context from your project.

The product has increasingly centered on code review. The AI Code Review Agent examines pull requests on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket, leaves comments on issues such as bugs, security problems, and style violations, and summarizes the change for reviewers. It builds a model of the codebase so its feedback accounts for how the changed code fits with the rest, which helps reduce noisy comments. Teams use it to speed up reviews and catch issues earlier.

item.title: Brave Leo
item.description: Leo sits in the browser’s sidebar and works with whatever page you are viewing. You can ask it to summarize an article or a long video transcript, explain a technical passage, extract key points from a PDF, or answer questions about the content, without copying text into a separate chatbot. It can also help write or rewrite text, translate, brainstorm, and answer general questions, with the option of using the web for current information.

item.title: CodeRabbit
item.description:
CodeRabbit acts as a first reviewer. When a developer opens a pull request, it reads the diff along with surrounding code, writes a summary of the change, and leaves comments on potential bugs, missing tests, security concerns, and style. Developers can reply to its comments and ask it to explain or fix things, so the review becomes a conversation.

Configuration lets teams set rules and instructions in plain language so the review follows their standards. It learns from feedback, and can run linters and security scanners as part of the review. IDE and command line versions bring review earlier, before a pull request is opened.

item.title: CodeRabbit
item.description:
CodeRabbit gives every pull request a quick first review. When a developer opens a pull request, it summarizes the change, walks through the files, and leaves comments on potential bugs, security problems, performance concerns, and deviations from team conventions. It can also suggest fixes that developers apply with a click and answer questions in the comments, acting like a tireless reviewer available at any hour.

It improves with use. CodeRabbit learns from how reviewers respond to its suggestions and from guidelines the team defines, so comments become more relevant over time. It runs linters and security scanners as part of its review, can use context from the wider codebase, and has an IDE and command-line version for reviewing before code is pushed. It integrates with issue trackers to check that changes match requirements.

item.title: Codiga
item.description:
Codiga offered real-time code analysis inside the editor. Its plugins for VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and other tools scanned code as you typed for security vulnerabilities, bugs, and violations of coding standards, and a rules engine let teams write their own checks. It also provided a code snippet assistant and, later, AI-based suggestions, and integrated with Git platforms to review pull requests automatically.

The company was acquired by Datadog, which wanted to bring code analysis into its observability and security platform. Codiga’s standalone products were shut down shortly afterward, with refunds for paid subscribers, and the team joined Datadog. The static analysis engine and its rules now underpin Datadog Code Security, and the analyzer is available as open source.

item.title: E2B
item.description:
E2B gives AI agents a safe computer. When a language model writes code, running it directly on a server is risky. E2B creates an isolated sandbox in the cloud, executes the code, returns the output and files, and shuts it down. Startup is fast enough to be used inside an agent loop.

Developers use its SDKs for Python and JavaScript to start sandboxes, run commands, read and write files, and stream results. It supports data analysis agents, coding assistants, and tools that need browsers or desktops, and templates define the environment. The core is open source and can be self-hosted.

item.title: Forta
item.description:
Forta provides security monitoring for blockchain applications. Independent developers write detection bots that scan transactions and state changes across networks, looking for patterns that signal attacks, such as sudden fund movements or unusual contract calls. Bots publish alerts to the network, which protocols and users can subscribe to.

Machine learning models are used for some detections, such as spotting scams or anomalies. Protocols use Forta alerts to trigger their own responses, such as pausing contracts. A marketplace of bots covers many threat types and chains, and its token supports staking and rewards for bot operators.

item.title: Harvey
item.description:
Harvey was built for lawyers and has become one of the best-known legal AI companies. Attorneys use its assistant to ask legal questions, draft and revise contracts and memos, summarize documents, and analyze large sets of files, such as the documents in a due diligence review. It runs on leading language models adapted for legal work and is designed to provide citations so lawyers can verify the answers.

Beyond a chat assistant, Harvey offers structured features. Vault stores and analyzes large document collections, workflows automate multi-step tasks such as contract review against a playbook, and integrations connect with tools law firms already use, including document management and legal research providers. Firms can customize the system with their own templates and precedents, and security controls support the confidentiality requirements of legal practice.

item.title: IBM Watson Government
item.description:
IBM Watson Government packages IBM’s AI offerings for the public sector. Agencies use them for tasks such as analyzing large volumes of text, extracting information from documents, supporting citizen service chatbots, and detecting fraud or anomalies in data. The emphasis is on meeting security and compliance standards that governments require.

The services run on IBM’s cloud and in hybrid environments, with options for on-premises deployment. Newer watsonx products add generative AI and governance tools for tracking models and risks, which agencies need under rules for responsible AI.

item.title: Kagi
item.description:
Kagi takes a different business model from other search engines: users pay a subscription, and in return there are no ads, no tracking-based profiles, and no incentive to favor advertisers. Results are meant to be clean and relevant, and the company says it does not sell data. The service uses several sources, including its own index of smaller sites, and puts effort into reducing low-quality content and SEO spam.

Control is a defining feature. Users can raise, lower, or block domains, so a site that is always useless for you disappears, and lenses restrict a search to a set of sources, such as forums or academic sites. AI tools include summaries of pages and videos, answers with citations, and an assistant that gives access to multiple language models. Kagi has also launched Orion, a privacy-focused browser, and other products around the search experience.

item.title: Microsoft Government Cloud
item.description:
Azure Government is a separate cloud region set up for US federal, state, and local agencies and their partners. It runs in data centers staffed by screened US personnel and is isolated from commercial Azure, which allows it to meet compliance regimes for sensitive government data.

Agencies use it for the usual range of cloud work, including hosting applications, analytics, and AI. Services such as Azure OpenAI and Copilot have been made available in versions that meet government requirements, which lets agencies use generative AI with data protections.

item.title: Palantir Gotham
item.description:
Gotham helps organizations that work with sensitive and scattered data make decisions. It pulls information from many systems, such as databases, reports, sensor feeds, and documents, into a unified model of people, places, events, and relationships, called an ontology. Analysts can search, visualize connections, map activity, and collaborate on investigations, and operational users can plan and track missions.

The platform is used in defense, intelligence, and public safety. Capabilities include link analysis, geospatial views, timelines, and tools for managing access to classified or restricted data, and it can run in secure and air-gapped environments. Palantir’s Artificial Intelligence Platform adds large language models that work with the same data under access controls, allowing users to ask questions and automate analysis.

item.title: Plaid
item.description: Plaid connects apps to bank accounts. When you link an account in a budgeting app, investment platform, or payments service, Plaid’s interface asks you to sign in to your bank, and the app then receives only the data you permit. Developers use Plaid’s APIs to verify account ownership, check balances, read transaction history, confirm identity, assess income and assets for lending, and initiate transfers, without building separate integrations with thousands of banks.

item.title: Semgrep
item.description:
Semgrep scans code for patterns. Rules look like the code they match, which makes them easier to write than traditional analyzers’ queries. Teams use community rules for common vulnerabilities and write custom ones for their own standards, running scans in CI and on developers’ machines.

The commercial platform adds dependency scanning, secrets detection, and a triage assistant that uses AI to explain findings, suggest fixes, and filter likely false positives. It integrates with pull requests and issue trackers.

item.title: Siri
item.description: Siri is the assistant that comes with every Apple device. You say “Hey Siri” or hold a button, then ask it to send a message, set a timer, call someone, play music, adjust a setting, or control HomeKit devices. It works across Apple’s hardware, so the same assistant is on your wrist, in your car through CarPlay, and on a smart speaker. Its biggest advantage is how deeply it ties into the system, since it can act on messages, calendars, reminders, and photos without extra setup.

item.title: Snyk AI
item.description:
Snyk puts security checks into the development workflow. Developers connect repositories and CI pipelines, and Snyk scans their own code, third-party libraries, container images, and cloud configuration for known vulnerabilities and insecure patterns, then reports issues with guidance. Findings appear in the IDE, pull requests, and dashboards, and automatic fix pull requests can upgrade vulnerable dependencies.

AI plays a central role. DeepCode AI, trained on security data, analyzes code and generates suggested fixes, and Snyk has developed tools to scan code written by AI coding assistants and to guard agents using the Model Context Protocol. As developers use assistants to write more code, automated security review becomes more important, and Snyk positions itself as a safety layer.

item.title: Tactiq
item.description:
Tactiq takes a lightweight approach to meeting notes. Instead of sending a recording bot into the call, it runs as a browser extension that captures the meeting’s captions and audio on your device. A live transcript appears in a sidebar as people speak, and you can highlight key moments as the meeting happens. That makes it less intrusive in calls where an unfamiliar bot would raise eyebrows.

After the meeting, AI features produce summaries, action items, and custom outputs from prompts, such as a follow-up email or a status update. The transcript is saved in your account and can be exported to tools like Notion, Google Docs, Slack, and HubSpot. Templates adapt the output for different meeting types, and a search function finds past conversations.

item.title: Topaz Video AI
item.description:
Topaz Video AI improves footage after it has been shot. Its models upscale low-resolution video to HD or 4K, remove noise and compression artifacts, and sharpen soft footage. Frame interpolation creates additional frames to make slow motion smoother or convert a low frame rate to a higher one, and stabilization steadies shaky shots. Archivists restoring old film and videographers rescuing difficult footage use it often.

Different models are tuned for different problems, such as live action, animation, or low-quality sources. Newer diffusion-based models aim for higher-quality enhancement of detail, at the cost of heavy processing. The app lets you preview results on short clips before processing a whole video, supports batch processing and command-line use, and exports to common formats, with some cloud options for heavy models.

item.title: Tray.io
item.description:
Tray.io builds on the idea of integration-platform-as-a-service. Teams use a visual builder to create workflows that connect SaaS applications, databases, and internal systems, with powerful logic, error handling, and the ability to write code where necessary. Hundreds of connectors and a universal connector for APIs cover common enterprise tools such as Salesforce, Workday, and Slack.

The company has moved toward AI agents. Its Merlin AI tools let teams build agents that use the connected systems as tools, so an agent can look up a customer, update a record, and send a message, with governance over what it can access. Embedded integration products let software companies offer customer-facing integrations in their own products.

item.title: Upscayl
item.description: Upscayl makes AI upscaling available to anyone. You drag in a low-resolution image, choose a model, and the app enlarges it by two, three, or four times with added detail, saving the result to your computer. It includes models tuned for general photos, digital art, and sharpening, and supports batch processing for many files. Because it runs on your own hardware, there is no per-image fee, and your images stay private.

item.title: Venice AI
item.description: Venice AI builds its pitch around privacy and freedom of use. The company states it does not log or store conversations on its servers, and that chats are kept in the user’s browser, which appeals to people uneasy about their prompts being retained or used for training. It runs open-source models, so users can pick from several language models and an image generator, and the platform applies fewer content restrictions than many mainstream services.

item.title: Voicemod
item.description: Voicemod changes how you sound as you speak. You choose a voice effect, such as a robot, a deep voice, or a character, and the app processes your microphone audio in real time. It works as a virtual microphone, so apps like Discord, Zoom, OBS, and many games treat it like a normal mic. Gamers and streamers use it for fun and for roleplay, and some people use it for privacy.

item.title: Yodlee
item.description:
Yodlee lets financial apps pull in customers’ account data. A budgeting tool, lender, or wealth platform can use Yodlee’s APIs to link to thousands of financial institutions, retrieve balances and transactions, and keep them updated. That saves each company from building separate connections to every bank.

Beyond raw data, Yodlee enriches transactions. Machine learning cleans merchant names, assigns categories, and flags patterns, and analytics products use aggregated data to describe consumer spending trends. Account verification and income checks help lenders confirm information, and the company supports open banking rules in regions where they exist.

item.title: You.com
item.description:
You.com is a search engine that mixes web results with AI-generated answers. You ask a question and receive a conversational response with links to sources, along with traditional results and apps for tasks like coding or image creation. A privacy focus has been part of its positioning, with a private mode and a commitment to not selling personal data.

The product has moved toward agents and enterprise search. Research and agent modes run multi-step investigations and produce longer reports, a custom agent builder lets people create assistants for specific tasks, and the platform lets users switch among models from different providers. For developers and businesses, You.com offers APIs that deliver live web search results formatted for AI applications, which several AI companies use to ground their answers.

item.title: Aleph Alpha
item.description: Aleph Alpha was Europe’s attempt to build a homegrown large language model company. Its Luminous models offered multilingual text generation and could handle images alongside text, with an emphasis on explainability, so users could see which parts of a source supported an answer. The company pitched itself to public sector agencies, banks, and industrial companies in Europe that wanted AI under their own control and in line with European regulation.

item.title: Darktrace
item.description: Darktrace takes a different approach from signature-based security. Instead of matching known threats, it learns the usual patterns of each organization, such as which devices talk to which systems and how people normally log in, and then notices when something deviates. This lets it detect novel attacks and insider threats that do not match a known signature. The learning happens inside the customer’s environment, and Darktrace says it does not need to share data with a central model to do it.

item.title: Lakera
item.description:
Lakera defends applications built on language models. Its Guard product sits between users and a model, scanning prompts for attempts to override instructions, extract secrets, or inject malicious content, and checking outputs for leaks and harmful material. Developers add it with an API call.

The company grew out of research on adversarial attacks and became known for Gandalf, a public game where players try to trick a model into revealing a password, which generated a large dataset of attacks. Red teaming tools test applications before launch.

item.title: Vectra AI
item.description:
Vectra focuses on attacker behavior inside a network. Its platform watches traffic, identities, and cloud logs, uses machine learning to spot patterns such as lateral movement or privilege abuse, and prioritizes the few detections that matter among thousands of alerts.

Security teams use it for threat detection and investigation across on-premises, cloud, and software-as-a-service environments, with integrations into SIEM and response tools. Managed services provide round-the-clock monitoring.

Vectra is sold to enterprises on subscription. Alert quality depends on tuning and coverage. Alternatives include Darktrace, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender XDR, ExtraHop, and Palo Alto Cortex. Vectra AI suits security operations teams.

item.title: Cohere
item.description:
Cohere sells AI to businesses and keeps its focus there. Its flagship Command models handle generation, summarization, and tool use, while Embed turns text into vectors for semantic search, and Rerank reorders search results by relevance. Together those pieces form the backbone of retrieval-augmented generation, where a model answers from a company’s own documents instead of from memory. Cohere also builds models for translation, document parsing, and speech transcription.

What differentiates it from OpenAI and Anthropic is how it is deployed. Cohere models can run on major clouds, in a customer’s private cloud, or fully on-premises, which suits banks, governments, and healthcare organizations that cannot send data to a public service. North is its workplace platform for AI agents that search company data and complete tasks, and Compass provides enterprise search. The company’s research arm also releases open-weight models for non-commercial use.

item.title: Collate
item.description:
Collate focuses on private document work. A user opens a PDF, such as a paper, contract, or textbook, and asks questions about it or requests a summary. Because the processing runs locally on the device, the document does not need to leave the computer, which matters for sensitive files.

Typical uses include studying, reviewing research papers, and pulling key terms from long reports. Local models are smaller than cloud models, so results are good for summaries and questions about the text but may be less strong on complex reasoning, and speed depends on the hardware.

item.title: Doximity
item.description:
Doximity is often described as LinkedIn for doctors. Physicians use it as a free directory and communication tool: they can find colleagues, send secure messages and faxes, and call patients using a number that shows the practice’s caller ID, all under a verified identity. Many of the country’s doctors have profiles, which makes it a convenient way to reach other clinicians for referrals and coordination.

The platform has added tools for clinical work. It provides medical news and journal feeds tailored to specialties, continuing education credits, telehealth video visits, and, increasingly, AI assistants for drafting letters, prior authorization appeals, and notes. A clinical reference tool answers questions drawn from medical sources. Doximity earns most of its revenue from pharmaceutical marketing and recruiting.

item.title: Kin Personal AI
item.description:
Kin positions itself as a private personal AI. Users talk with an assistant that remembers their circumstances and offers guidance across areas of life, with specialized advisors that focus on different topics. The conversation builds a profile over time so advice reflects what the user has shared.

Privacy is the main selling point. The company states that personal data is stored locally on the device and encrypted, rather than in a central cloud, so sensitive details are less exposed. This appeals to people who want to discuss personal matters without handing data to a large platform.

item.title: Logseq
item.description: Logseq is built on the idea that notes should be a network of connected blocks. You write in an outliner where each bullet is a block, link to other pages with double brackets, and see backlinks that show everywhere an idea is referenced. Daily journals are the default entry point, so you capture thoughts as they come and organize them through links instead of folders. A graph view shows how pages relate.

item.title: Reflect
item.description:
Reflect aims to be a quick place to capture thoughts and connect them. You write notes, link them to each other with simple syntax, and see backlinks that show where an idea is referenced. Daily notes serve as an inbox, a calendar view ties notes to meetings, and a graph helps visualize connections. The app is built for speed and a clean interface, with sync across devices.

The AI assistant works on your notes. It can summarize a page, rewrite text, brainstorm, and answer questions based on the content you have saved, and voice transcription turns spoken notes into text. Reflect also emphasizes privacy: notes are end-to-end encrypted, which limits what the company can see. Browser extensions and integrations let you save web content and connect with services like Kindle highlights and Readwise.

item.title: Slack AI
item.description:
Slack AI addresses the problem of catching up. When you return from time off or join a busy channel, it can summarize what happened, list decisions, and highlight what needs your attention. Thread summaries cut long discussions into a few lines, and daily recaps cover channels you choose, so you can stay informed without reading every message.

AI search turns Slack into a place to ask questions. Instead of hunting for keywords, you can ask something like what the timeline is for a project, and receive an answer drawn from messages, files, and connected apps, with links to the sources. Slackbot is being reshaped as an assistant that can help draft messages, find information, and take actions, and Salesforce’s Agentforce agents can work in Slack. Huddle notes summarize audio calls.
